01 / Explore tasks

A small task. A concrete result.

Choose by interest and time. Every task is suitable for getting started; none requires personal data or field work.

6 tasks available

D60 min · A place to start

Check three public sources

Turn a list of links into a table another person can verify.

You will deliver

A 3-source table: institution, URL, purpose, consultation date and limitations.

See scope and review criteria

Ready for review when…

  • Every link leads to the expected institutional domain.
  • Each row separates what was checked from what remains uncertain.
  • No personal data or unsupported claims about service availability are included.

Keep it within scope

Do not contact affected people or test forms with real data. A reachable page does not prove a service is operational.

02 / Get started

From interest to a first draft.

You can read, practise and prepare a public-data example independently. Before investing more time, confirm the task is still useful and someone can review it.

  1. 01

    Choose a task

    Read its brief. Check the scope, expected result and what is excluded. You can start without prior experience.

  2. 02

    Introduce yourself and confirm

    Share the task and your availability on Discord or open a GitHub proposal. Ask to confirm priority and find a reviewer; do not publish personal data.

  3. 03

    Share a reviewable draft

    Include your result, sources and dates, how to check it and what you still do not know. An honest draft is a useful contribution.

Edit this text and share it on Discord. This page does not send or save it. If the invitation does not work, use a GitHub proposal.

No GitHub account? Prepare the same draft as a document and agree on delivery through Discord.

03 / When sharing your draft

Make your work useful to the next person.

A contribution is reviewed for clarity, verifiability and care, rather than how ambitious it sounds.

Sources and dates

Link to the origin of every claim and record when you consulted it. Say when you could not verify something.

A reviewable result

Share the file, link or change and steps to check it. Explain its limits.

Fair credit

Record what each person contributed. Authorship and order must reflect contributions and be agreed; first authorship, a DOI, mentorship and prizes are not guaranteed.

Privacy from the start

Exclude victims’ names, private contacts, clinical records, children’s data and locations of vulnerable people.

05 / The plan

The purpose, clearly stated.

Conexión RedJIV is a proposal connected to the Network of Young Venezuelan Researchers (RedJIV), a group of ACFIMAN. It aims to connect students and researchers with useful, remote scientific contributions.

Public plan (.md) ↓

The original context was the response to the June 2026 earthquakes in Venezuela. This page does not publish casualty counts or real-time alerts. Consult institutional sources for current information.

The proposed model is distributed work with small, reviewable deliverables. Meetings, review availability and any follow-up work must be confirmed with the community. This page confirms neither a start date nor funding.

The network can contribute documentation, sources, reproducible code and open-data analysis. It does not provide rescue, diagnoses, clinical care or building-safety assessments. Health, water and hazard materials require specialist review before any operational use.

Six routes to orient the work

A

The backbone

Documentation, organisation and contribution.

B

Maps and needs

Learn from existing mapping, without creating registries of people.

C

Clean water

Review public sources; practical guidance requires expert review.

D

Ecosystem and data

Verify sources and make reproducible analyses.

E

Health and wellbeing

Bibliography and communication; clinical use requires safeguards and review.

F

Safe ground

Sources and education; safety recommendations belong with specialists.

FAQ

Before you start

Do I need to code?

No. Critical reading, translation, documentation, accessibility reviews and source checking are useful contributions. Each brief lists the tools needed.

Will this count toward my studies?

It can help you build a portfolio of public contributions. Academic credit, certificates and recognition must be agreed with your institution and are not guaranteed.

Is a mentor assigned to every task?

Availability is not guaranteed. Ask for a reviewer before expanding the work. In the meantime, use the briefs as independent exercises with public sources.

Can I use AI?

Yes, as support, if you explain how you used it and verify the results. Do not enter personal or private data or submit invented references.

Can I report an emergency here?

No. Do not post personal cases or urgent requests in issues, pull requests or Discord. Use local official services.
